You are an assistant helping a developer with their CircleCI projects. Answer the user's question using only the tools provided to you. Ground every claim in data you actually retrieved; if you cannot retrieve something, say so. Do not change anything in the project beyond what the user explicitly asks for. Finish with a clear, direct answer to the question.

The current directory is a checkout of the CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli repository. You can inspect its files with the read-only list_files and read_file tools.

This server exposes CircleCI: the CI pipelines an org runs, the deploys those
pipelines produce, and the config, orbs, functions and usage data around them. Every tool
acts as the authenticated user and sees only what that user can see.

Ids are UUIDs and are not interchangeable — a run id, a workflow id and a job
id are distinct, and a tool handed the wrong kind fails rather than guessing.
Nothing accepts a job number or a CircleCI web URL. Projects and orgs are the
exception: they take either a slug ("gh/org/repo", "gh/org") or a UUID.

SKILLS. This server ships written playbooks for the work that takes several
of the tools below — the orderings, the costs and the usual mistakes, which
no single tool description can carry:

    list_skills  the catalog: what each playbook covers, and its references
    get_skill    one playbook, or one of its bundled references

Before working through the tools below, call list_skills once and load any
skill whose description covers the work, together with the related skills it
names. It takes no arguments and returns the whole catalog, so that one call
is the entire search. If nothing clearly fits, load nothing and work from the
tool descriptions. One pass serves a whole session: having listed once, do not
list again. The one exception is a failed run you hold the id of: call
get_run_failure_report first, and look for a skill only if it leaves the
cause open.

A skill earns its call at the start of a piece of work, not after one has gone
wrong. The same guides are readable as resources under circleci://skills/ for
clients that browse resources rather than call tools.

PIPELINES. The tools form a chain, each level's id feeding the next:

    list_runs -> get_run -> list_run_workflows -> get_workflow -> list_workflow_jobs -> get_job

Enter at list_runs; it is the only one of these that takes a project rather
than a UUID. With no project named, mine=true lists the user's own runs across
every project. Skip levels whenever you already hold an id — get_run is
pointless if you have the run id and want its workflows. trigger_run starts a
new run and returns its id, which enters the chain at get_run.

If you hold a run id and want to know why it failed, call
get_run_failure_report first; you do not need list_skills or any tool in the
chain before it. It walks the chain in one call and returns the failed steps
with their exit codes and condensed output, plus the job id, execution and step
num the tools below take; on a very wide run it says what it left out. Reach
for those tools only for what the report leaves open.

For the files a run stored — a coverage report, test results, a build
output — call list_run_artifacts with the run id rather than walking the chain
and calling list_job_artifacts once per job: it reads every job's artifacts in
one call, and path narrows them to the ones wanted. For the latest successful
run, take the id from list_runs with status "success" and limit 1.

DIAGNOSING A JOB. Five tools take a job id and answer different questions.
Which you pick matters more than the order:

    get_job                 which step failed and its exit code, or why it never ran
    list_job_tests          which tests failed
    get_job_logs            what a step printed
    get_job_resource_usage  whether it ran out of CPU or memory
    list_job_artifacts      the files it persisted, with download URLs

Start with get_job — it is cheap and names the failed step — unless
get_run_failure_report already did. If that step ran
tests, go to list_job_tests, which is far cheaper than logs and already
filtered to failures. Reach for get_job_logs only when you need the output
itself; it is the most expensive tool here, so keep tail_lines small. If a job
died with nothing in its logs, check get_job_resource_usage for an OOM.

FLAKY TESTS. list_flaky_tests takes a project, not a job, and answers "which
tests are flaky?" in one call: tests that failed and then passed within the
same pipeline, counted across the project's runs, most-flaked first. Reach for
it instead of walking runs and jobs to compare outcomes, and to check whether
a test that just failed is a known flake before treating it as a regression.

DEPLOYS are a separate subsystem, keyed on projects and orgs rather than on
pipeline ids, and reachable without touching a run:

    list_deployments                what was deployed — to a project, or across an org
    list_deploy_components          a project's deployable units
    list_deploy_environments        an org's release targets (production, staging)
    list_deploy_component_versions  a component's version history
    get_deploy_component            one component by id
    get_deploy_environment          one environment by id

For "what is live" or "when did X ship", use list_deployments — pass project for
a single project or org for everything in the org. The two get_ tools resolve an
id you already hold back to its name; the list tools already return names, so reach
for them only when an id arrived from somewhere else.

CONFIG, ORBS AND FUNCTIONS need no CircleCI resource at all; they work on YAML
you hold:

    validate_config  compile a config and report its errors
    get_orb          an orb's published versions — whether a pin is stale
    get_orb_source   an orb's YAML — how to call its jobs and commands
    list_functions   every published function, with its versions
    get_function     one function's arguments, versions, and the config that uses it

Read an orb's source before writing config against it, and compile a config
before pushing it rather than after. To add a function, take the declaration
and step get_function returns and edit the config yourself: nothing here
writes to it.

When writing a new config, or adding a setup or test step to one, call
list_functions first and use the matching function; write a run: step
only when none fits. Orbs remain supported for existing pipelines, so do
not move a working orb-based config to functions unless the user asks.

WRITES. trigger_run is additive: it starts a new run of a project's branch or tag.
rerun_workflow is additive: it creates a new workflow. cancel_workflow
stops running work. rollback_deploy_component redeploys production software.
Confirm with the user before calling any of them unless they asked for it
directly — and for a rollback, confirm the component, the environment and both
versions rather than just the intent.

Also: get_me for the authenticated user's identity and ids, and
download_usage_data for an org's billing CSVs (asynchronous — start an export,
then poll it).

FEEDBACK. send_feedback reports a problem with this server to CircleCI — an
error that looks like CircleCI's fault, a capability that is missing, or a
tool that misled you. Errors that look like CircleCI's fault end by pointing
to it. Report once per distinct problem, saying what you were trying to do and
what happened. It changes nothing in CircleCI, so unlike the writes above it
needs no confirmation. Report functions too: when you write a run: step
because no function does the job, or because one falls short, send it with
type and function.

When a tool errors, read the message before retrying. Most errors here say
what was wrong — the wrong kind of id, a missing project, an execution index
out of range — and the same arguments will fail the same way.

## Available skills

Skills are packaged instructions for specific kinds of tasks. The following skills are available:

- circleci-builds: Diagnose and fix failing CircleCI builds quickly and safely. Use when users ask to investigate failed CircleCI jobs, triage flaky pipelines, identify root causes from logs, and implement minimal fixes in configuration, test setup, or build-related code paths.
- circleci-cli: Day-to-day CircleCI from the terminal with the circleci CLI — authenticate, validate config before you commit, watch the run your push triggered, review pipeline/workflow/job status, print a failure report for your latest failed run in one command, read job logs and failed tests, list a project's flaky tests, list or download every artifact in a run in one command, and rerun/cancel/trigger. Use when a developer asks to authenticate CLI access, check their build or pipeline status, watch a run after pushing, see why CI failed, read job output/logs, find failing tests, list flaky tests, download build outputs such as a coverage report, rerun failed jobs, cancel or re-trigger a run, validate a config change locally, or look up a project's environment variables, contexts, triggers or pipeline definitions. For first-time project connection / pipeline-definition setup use the onboarding skill; for the diagnose-and-fix methodology on a failing build use circleci-builds.
- circleci-config: Optimize CircleCI configuration for speed, reliability, and maintainability. Use when users ask to improve `.circleci/config.yml`, reduce CI runtime, tune caching/workspaces/parallelism, remove pipeline waste, or fix flaky pipeline behavior caused by configuration choices.
- circleci-deploy-setup: Set up, audit, or regenerate CircleCI deploy markers, deploy and rollback pipelines, and release validation in a repository. Use when a user wants to onboard a project to deploys, releases, deploy markers, smart deployments, release validation or auto-rollback; when they ask what deploy setup a repo already has or whether it is complete; when they want to regenerate or upgrade an existing deploy.yml, rollback.yml, or marker setup; or when they ask to replicate the Deploys setup wizard locally. Covers config generation, verification, pipeline registration, and wiring validation webhooks from Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Alertmanager, or any tool that can POST to a URL. For first-time project connection and basic pipeline setup use the onboarding skill.
- circleci-smarter-testing-debugging: Debug CircleCI Smarter Testing on a project that is already onboarded, using `circleci testsuite impact` to explore impact data (which files impact a test, which tests a file impacts) and `circleci testsuite result` to show how a job's test atoms were selected and how they ran. Use when asking why a test was selected or skipped, why a change didn't run the expected tests, why too many tests run, or how a test atom ran in a job. For first-time setup use circleci-smarter-testing-onboarding.
- circleci-smarter-testing-onboarding: Onboard a project onto CircleCI Smarter Testing — check the default suite for the detected test runner (or write `.circleci/test-suites.yml` when it doesn't fit), replace the raw test step (or legacy `circleci tests glob`/`split`/`run`) with `circleci testsuite run`, validate with `circleci testsuite doctor`, make sure the free features work (static test splitting, rerun only failed tests, test uploads), then ask if any credit-charged features should be enabled (test impact analysis, dynamic test splitting, dynamic parallelism, auto rerun failed tests). Use for first-time setup of Smarter Testing, testsuite, test-suites YAML, or migrating a test step. Not for running (circleci-smarter-testing-run) or debugging a suite that is already onboarded.
- circleci-smarter-testing-run: Run a project's tests locally through CircleCI Smarter Testing with `circleci testsuite run`, which detects the test runner when there is no `.circleci/test-suites.yml`, narrowed to a subset with `--test-atom-pattern`, instead of calling the test runner directly. Use whenever you are about to run tests (`go test`, `npm test`, `pytest`, `jest`, `vitest`, `rspec`, `gradle test` and so on) in a repository that has `.circleci/test-suites.yml` or `.circleci/config.yml`, including running one package, file or directory of tests while iterating. For first-time setup use circleci-smarter-testing-onboarding; for why a test was selected or skipped use circleci-smarter-testing-debugging.
- debug-ci-failures: Debug CircleCI build failures, analyze test results, and identify flaky tests. Use when the user says "debug CI", "why is CI failing", "fix CI failures", "find flaky tests", "what broke in CI", "check CircleCI", or asks about failing pipelines or build errors.
- onboarding: Agent-driven onboarding guide for CircleCI. version: 2.1

functions:
  setup-go: github.com/circleci-functions/setup-go@v0.6.0

commands:
  setup:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - install-go
      - install-task

  # Installs the toolchain and restores the module, build and lint caches, saved at job end.
  install-go:
    steps:
      - setup-go:
          with:
            version-file: go.mod
            golangci-lint-cache: true
            checksum: '{{ checksum "go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "clikit/go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "tools/go.sum" }}'
      - run: go version

  install-task:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Install go-task
          command: |
            sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d -b "$HOME/.local/bin"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"

  # GoReleaser's dockers_v2 pipe shells out to `docker buildx build`, so the
  # builder and the registry login have to exist before it runs.
  setup-docker:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Register QEMU for cross-architecture builds
          # Dockerfile.alpine RUNs `apk add`, once per platform in the manifest,
          # so building its arm64 half on an amd64 host needs binfmt handlers
          # registered. Idempotent, and a no-op for the cimg/base image, which
          # only COPYs.
          command: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
      - run:
          name: Create a buildx builder
          # The machine image's default buildx driver is `docker`, which can
          # neither build for two platforms in one invocation nor push a
          # manifest list. A docker-container driver can do both.
          command: docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container
      - run:
          name: Log in to Docker Hub
          # Absent on branch dry-runs, which have no context: the snapshot build
          # still exercises the Dockerfile, it just pushes nothing.
          command: |
            if [ -z "${DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME:-}" ]; then
              echo "No Docker Hub credentials — skipping login (snapshot builds do not push)."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "$DOCKER_HUB_PASSWORD" | docker login --username "$DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" --password-stdin

  store_results:
    steps:
      - store_test_results:
          path: ./test-reports

executors:
  linux:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: large.gen3

  # Arm64 counterpart to `linux`, for checking both halves of a multi-arch
  # image. Deliberately small: it only pulls and runs a container.
  linux-arm:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: arm.medium

  macos:
    macos:
      xcode: 26.5.0

  windows:
    machine: true
    resource_class: windows.medium

jobs:
  check:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:check
      - store_results

  test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:test
      - store_results

  deploy:
    executor: linux
    parameters:
      # Run before anything is installed, so a push with nothing to release
      # stops cheaply.
      gate_steps:
        type: steps
        default: []
      publish_steps:
        type: steps
        default:
          - run: task ci:release
    steps:
      - setup
      - steps: << parameters.gate_steps >>
      - setup-docker
      - run: sudo apt update --yes
      - run:
          name: Install snapcraft
          command: |
            sudo apt install snapd --yes
            sudo snap install snapcraft --classic
      - run:
          name: Install choco
          command: |
            sudo cp tools/choco.sh /usr/local/bin/choco
            sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/choco
            choco help
      - steps: << parameters.publish_steps >>
      - store_artifacts:
          path: dist

  smoke-test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
      install-steps:
        type: steps
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - steps: << parameters.install-steps >>
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci binary
          command: circleci version

  # needs a machine of its own, so each job checks both variants. Printing the
  # arch inside the container makes the log say which half of the manifest ran. A
  # tag missing this platform fails here anyway — the arm machine images carry no
  # binfmt, so there is nothing to silently emulate an amd64-only image with.
  smoke-test-docker:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1 sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'

  # Opens or updates the release PR (see RELEASE.md).
  release-pr:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:release-pr

  docs:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run:
          name: Generate reference and build the site
          command: task docs:build
      - run:
          name: Check internal links
          command: task docs:test
      - store_artifacts:
          path: docs/website/public
      - persist_to_workspace:
          root: .
          paths:
            - "docs/website/public"

  docs-publish:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      - run:
          name: Publish to gh-pages
          command: task ci:docs:publish

  ok-to-deploy:
    type: no-op

workflows:
  ci:
    jobs:
      # gh-pages holds only generated HTML — never run CI on it. Entry jobs (no
      # `requires`) must opt out explicitly; downstream jobs are gated by these.

      - check:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - test:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - macos
                - windows
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - docs:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - deploy:
          name: dry-run
          publish_steps:
            - run: task ci:build
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore:
                - main
                - gh-pages

      - ok-to-deploy:
          requires:
            - check
            - test
            - docs
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - release-pr:
          # One at a time, so two pushes can't race to rewrite release/next.
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/release-pr
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      # Publishes only on the push that merges the release PR; halts otherwise.
      - deploy:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/deploy
          gate_steps:
            - run:
                name: Halt unless the release is unpublished
                command: task ci:halt-unless-unreleased
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release
            - macos-codesigning

      - docs-publish:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/docs-publish
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-snap
          executor: linux
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install snapd
                command: sudo apt update --yes && sudo apt install snapd --yes
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Snap stable channel
                # /snap/bin has to be prepended, not just present: the machine
                # image ships its own circleci in /usr/local/bin, which would
                # otherwise shadow the snap and make this job verify the build
                # agent's CLI instead of the release.
                command: |

                  echo 'export PATH="/snap/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-brew
          executor: macos
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Homebrew preview tap
                command: |
                  brew update
                  rm -f /opt/homebrew/bin/circleci
                  brew install circleci-public/circleci/circleci@next
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test-docker:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - linux-arm
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-choco
          executor: windows
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Chocolatey
                command: choco install circleci-cli -y
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

# Skill: circleci-config

# CircleCI Config

## Overview

Use this skill to improve CircleCI performance and stability without changing product behavior. Focus on measured bottlenecks first, then implement the smallest safe config changes with clear validation criteria.

Read `references/cache-optimization.md` when the request involves `save_cache`, `restore_cache`, `persist_to_workspace`, `attach_workspace`, cache key design, dependency caching, lockfiles, or complaints about low cache hit rates, oversized caches, or wasted persistence steps.
Read `references/persisting-data.md` when the request involves choosing between caches, workspaces, and artifacts, or when data is being moved between jobs inefficiently.
Read `references/test-results.md` when the request involves slow test jobs, parallelism, tests timings, or missing JUnit XML.
Read `references/patterns.md` when the request involves approvals, branch/tag filters, schedules, deploy flow structure, or environment promotion patterns.

## Inputs To Gather

- `.yaml` and `.yml` files in `.circleci/` and any reusable config fragments
- Current pain points: duration, flakiness, cost, or maintainability
- Baseline metrics: slowest jobs, most frequent retries/failures, queue and run times
- Risk tolerance for structural changes

## Workflow

1. Build a baseline.
   - Identify top 1-3 longest jobs and top flaky jobs.
   - Capture before metrics (duration, pass rate, retries).
2. Remove pipeline waste.
   - Eliminate duplicate jobs/workflows.
   - Tighten branch/tag filters and workflow triggers.
3. Improve dependency and artifact flow.
   - Fix cache keys to include deterministic lockfile checks.
   - Use workspaces/artifacts to avoid rebuilding identical outputs.
   - Prefer cache scopes that are narrow, reproducible, and cheap to restore.
4. Apply safe parallelism.
   - Parallelize only proven bottlenecks.
   - Keep fan-out/fan-in readable and deterministic.
5. Validate impact.
   - Define expected metric changes and acceptance criteria before finalizing.

## Guardrails

- Prefer configuration fixes before proposing application code changes.
- When adding a new job or setup step, check `circleci function list` (or `list_functions`) first. Don't move a working pipeline's orbs to Functions unless the user asks.
- Do not add blanket retries to hide deterministic failures.
- Preserve deployment safety gates while optimizing build/test stages.
- Keep changes incremental and easy to revert.
- Prefer language-specific cache directories over broad project snapshots.
- Avoid cache keys that rotate every run unless the user explicitly wants effectively write-only caches.

## Output Contract

Provide:

1. Baseline bottleneck summary.
2. Proposed or applied config changes with rationale.
3. Expected runtime/reliability impact.
4. Validation plan and rollback note.

{"content":"# Work on a CircleCI config

Two habits carry almost all of the value here, and both replace a guess with a
call:

1. **Read an orb before calling it.** `get_orb_source` returns the definition
   that will actually run — every job, command, executor and parameter, with
   their defaults. No orb documentation is reachable through this server, and an
   invented parameter name is a compile error at best and a silently ignored
   value at worst.
2. **Compile the config before pushing it.** `validate_config` runs the same
   compilation the platform runs when a pipeline starts. Found here it costs one
   call; found by pushing it costs a run, a wait, and a red branch.

## What you need to start

The config itself — read `.circleci/config.yml` out of the checkout rather than
reconstructing it from memory — and, if it declares private or URL orbs, the
org:

    git remote get-url origin      # git@github.com:org/repo.git -> gh/org

Nothing in this skill needs a project, a run, or any CircleCI id. These tools
work on YAML you are holding, which is what makes the loop below cheap enough
to run on every edit.

## 1. For a new config or a new setup step, check for a Function

    list_functions

If one matches, use it: get_function returns the exact lines to add, the
functions: entry and the step. Write a run: step only if none fits. If the
config already uses orbs, keep them unless the user asks to switch.

## 2. Read the orbs before touching them

The `orbs:` stanza names each orb and pins it. Everything the config then
invokes under that name — `go/test`, `slack/notify` — is defined somewhere you
cannot see from the repo:

    get_orb_source {orb: "circleci/go@1.2.3"}

That is the YAML that runs. Read the `jobs:`, `commands:`, `executors:` and
`parameters:` blocks in it to learn the interface: what a job is called, which
parameters it takes, which have defaults and which are required.

    get_orb {orb: "circleci/go"}

That is the version history — the latest published version, and every stable
version before it. Use it to answer "is this pin stale" and "what should it
move to", never to guess at the interface.

Both tools take registry orbs only, as `namespace/name`. Inline orbs are in the
config you already hold; URL orbs are not readable through either tool, so the
config is the only description of them you get.

There is no orb search here. If you do not know an orb's `namespace/name`, you
cannot discover it through this server — ask, or read it from a config that
already uses it.

See `references/orbs.md` for pinning, dev versions, and what a private orb
changes.

## 3. Make the change

Ordinary YAML editing, with the orb source open. Two things worth knowing
before you write:

- A parameter you invented is not a compile error in every position — an
  unknown key under a job invocation can be accepted and then ignored, which
  looks like a working config that does nothing. The source is the only place
  that says which keys exist.
- `<< >>` expressions are resolved at compile time, not at run time, so a
  pipeline parameter with no default and no value is a compilation failure
  rather than a runtime one. Step 4 can supply values for them.

## 4. Compile it before pushing

    validate_config {config: "<the whole file>", org: "gh/org"}

`valid: true` means it compiled. `valid: false` returns `errors`, each naming
the problem and usually the line.

**Always pass `org` when the config declares private registry orbs or URL
orbs.** Without it, only public orbs resolve, and you get errors like:

    orb not found
    not permitted by the organization's URL orb allow-list

Those are **false negatives from missing org context, not config problems.**
Before reporting a config invalid, check whether it declares a private or URL
orb, and if so retry with `org`. Reporting a working config as broken because
`org` was omitted is the most common way to waste someone's time with these
tools.

Three more arguments, for configs that need context to compile:

| Argument | For |
| --- | --- |
| `pipeline_parameters` | `<< pipeline.parameters.* >>` — a map of parameter name to value. Needed for any parameter declared without a default. |
| `pipeline_values` | The wider `<< pipeline.* >>` context — `pipeline.git.branch` and friends — as a flat map. Usually unnecessary. |
| `preview_next` | Compile against upcoming, potentially breaking config changes. Use it to check a config will survive them, not as a default. |

Validate the **whole file**, not the fragment you edited. Compilation is
whole-config: an anchor, an alias, or a `requires` reference to a job elsewhere
in the file only resolves when the rest of it is there.

Then iterate: fix, validate, repeat. Each cycle is one call.

## 5. After it is pushed

A config that fails to compile produces a run with `errors` and **no
workflows** — there is no job to look at, which is why a config error looks
like nothing happened:

    list_runs {project: "gh/org/repo", branch: "my-branch", limit: 5}

If the run carries `errors`, feed the same config back through
`validate_config` to reproduce them locally and fix from there. If it produced
workflows but a job failed, the config compiled and the problem is in what it
asked for — `debug-failing-run` is the skill for that.

## Report what changed, and what you checked

Say what you edited, that it compiles (and with which `org` and parameters, if
those mattered), and which orb version's source you read to write it. A config
change reported as "should work" without a `validate_config` call behind it is
a guess, and this is the one server where checking is nearly free.

## Reference

- `references/orbs.md` — pinning and version selection, dev and volatile
  versions, private and URL orbs, and reading an orb's interface out of its
  source.

version: 2.1

functions:
  setup-go: github.com/circleci-functions/setup-go@v0.6.0

commands:
  setup:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - install-go
      - install-task

  # Installs the toolchain and restores the module, build and lint caches, saved at job end.
  install-go:
    steps:
      - setup-go:
          with:
            version-file: go.mod
            golangci-lint-cache: true
            checksum: '{{ checksum "go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "clikit/go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "tools/go.sum" }}'
      - run: go version

  install-task:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Install go-task
          command: |
            sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d -b "$HOME/.local/bin"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"

  setup-docker:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Register QEMU for cross-architecture builds
          command: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
      - run:
          name: Create a buildx builder
          command: docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container
      - run:
          name: Log in to Docker Hub
          command: |
            if [ -z "${DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME:-}" ]; then
              echo "No Docker Hub credentials — skipping login (snapshot builds do not push)."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "$DOCKER_HUB_PASSWORD" | docker login --username "$DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" --password-stdin

  store_results:
    steps:
      - store_test_results:
          path: ./test-reports

executors:
  linux:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: large.gen3

  linux-arm:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: arm.medium

  macos:
    macos:
      xcode: 26.5.0

  windows:
    machine: true
    resource_class: windows.medium

jobs:
  check:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:check
      - store_results

  test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:test
      - store_results

  deploy:
    executor: linux
    parameters:
      gate_steps:
        type: steps
        default: []
      publish_steps:
        type: steps
        default:
          - run: task ci:release
    steps:
      - setup
      - steps: << parameters.gate_steps >>
      - setup-docker
      - run: sudo apt update --yes
      - run:
          name: Install snapcraft
          command: |
            sudo apt install snapd --yes
            sudo snap install snapcraft --classic
      - run:
          name: Install choco
          command: |
            sudo cp tools/choco.sh /usr/local/bin/choco
            sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/choco
            choco help
      - steps: << parameters.publish_steps >>
      - store_artifacts:
          path: dist

  smoke-test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
      install-steps:
        type: steps
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - steps: << parameters.install-steps >>
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci binary
          command: circleci version

  smoke-test-docker:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1 sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'

  release-pr:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:release-pr

  docs:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run:
          name: Generate reference and build the site
          command: task docs:build
      - run:
          name: Check internal links
          command: task docs:test
      - store_artifacts:
          path: docs/website/public
      - persist_to_workspace:
          root: .
          paths:
            - "docs/website/public"

  docs-publish:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      - run:
          name: Publish to gh-pages
          command: task ci:docs:publish

  ok-to-deploy:
    type: no-op

workflows:
  ci:
    jobs:
      - check:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - test:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - macos
                - windows
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - docs:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - deploy:
          name: dry-run
          publish_steps:
            - run: task ci:build
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore:
                - main
                - gh-pages

      - ok-to-deploy:
          requires:
            - check
            - test
            - docs
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - release-pr:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/release-pr
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - deploy:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/deploy
          gate_steps:
            - run:
                name: Halt unless the release is unpublished
                command: task ci:halt-unless-unreleased
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release
            - macos-codesigning

      - docs-publish:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/docs-publish
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-snap
          executor: linux
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install snapd
                command: sudo apt update --yes && sudo apt install snapd --yes
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Snap stable channel
                command: |
                  sudo snap install circleci
                  echo 'export PATH="/snap/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-brew
          executor: macos
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Homebrew preview tap
                command: |
                  brew update
                  rm -f /opt/homebrew/bin/circleci
                  brew install circleci-public/circleci/circleci@next
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test-docker:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - linux-arm
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-choco
          executor: windows
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Chocolatey
                command: choco install circleci-cli -y
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

version: '3'

vars:
  RESULTS_DIR: test-reports
  TEST_REPORT: test-reports/tests.xml
  LINT_REPORT: test-reports/lint.xml

  # Hugo project lives in docs/website/; built output lands in docs/website/public.
  SITE_DIR: docs/website
  SITE_OUT: docs/website/public

  GH_NAME: 'circleci'
  GH_EMAIL: 'ops+deploy-bot@circleci.com'

  # Release version: the newest "## [x.y.z]" heading in CHANGELOG.md (see
  # RELEASE.md). Keep the pattern in step with sectionHeading in cmd/ci/release.
  #
  # No pre-release suffix: these are full releases, marked latest on GitHub and
  # published to the stable channel of every package manager.
  RELEASE_VERSION:
    sh: sed -n -E 's/^## \[([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)\].*/v\1/p' CHANGELOG.md | head -n 1

tasks:
  build:
    desc: Build the circleci binary
    vars:
      DEST: '{{default "dist/circleci" .DEST}}'
      # git describe --long against the last CLI release tag, e.g.
      # 1.12.0-5-gd4823563, which the update check reads as ahead of 1.12.0 and
      # so never nags about it. --long keeps the -N-g<sha> part even on a tag, so
      # a source build never passes for the release binary. --match skips the
      # clikit/vX.Y.Z tag on the same commit and --exclude skips -pre tags.
      # -dirty comes from git status, not describe --dirty, so untracked files
      # count. Without a reachable tag (a shallow or --no-tags clone) the
      # version is "dev", which skips the update check; the build warns.
      VERSION:
        sh: |
          v=$(git describe --tags --long --match 'v[0-9]*' --exclude 'v*-*' 2>/dev/null) || { echo dev; exit 0; }
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" || v="$v-dirty"
          echo "${v#v}"
    cmds:
      - cmd: >-
          echo 'warning: no CLI release tag reachable, stamping version "dev" (update checks off). Run `git fetch --tags` to fix.' >&2
        if: '[ "{{.VERSION}}" = dev ]'
      - go build -ldflags="-X main.version={{.VERSION}}" -o "{{.DEST}}" ./cmd/circleci

  release-check:
    desc: Check if the release is ready to be published
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod goreleaser check

  test:
    desc: Run unit tests
    # clikit is a separate module, so ./... does not reach it. A relative
    # ./clikit/... is rejected as outside the main module, but the module path
    # resolves through the replace in go.mod.
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./... github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/clikit/..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod gotestsum -- -race -count=1 {{.ARGS}}

  check:
    desc: Run all static checks
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: fmt:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: lint
      - task: lint:clikit
      - task: license
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -check .
      - task: mod-tidy
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -diff
      - task: release-check

  fix:
    desc: Auto-fix static checks
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
      - task: fmt:clikit
      - task: license
      - task: mod-tidy
      - task: lint
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --fix
      - task: lint:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --fix

  lint:
    desc: Run golangci-lint
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod golangci-lint run {{.ARGS}}

  lint:clikit:
    desc: Run golangci-lint on the clikit module
    dir: clikit
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile ../tools/go.mod golangci-lint run {{.ARGS}}

  fmt:
    desc: Format the code
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod golangci-lint fmt {{.ARGS}}

  fmt:clikit:
    desc: Format the clikit module
    dir: clikit
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile ../tools/go.mod golangci-lint fmt {{.ARGS}}

  license:
    desc: Manage license headers
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - |
        go tool -modfile tools/go.mod addlicense \
          -c "Circle Internet Services, Inc." \
          -l mit \
          -s \
          -ignore ".idea/**" \
          -ignore ".circleci/**" \
          -ignore ".claude/**" \
          -ignore ".git/**" \
          -ignore ".github/**" \
          -ignore "test-reports/**" \
          -ignore "**/*.html" \
          -ignore "acceptance/testdata/**" \
          -ignore "bin/**" \
          -ignore "dist/**" \
          -ignore "docs/website/content/**" \
          -ignore "docs/website/public/**" \
          {{.ARGS}}

  mod-tidy:
    desc: Run 'go mod tidy'
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "-v" .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go mod tidy {{.ARGS}}
      - go -C clikit mod tidy {{.ARGS}}
      - go -C tools mod tidy {{.ARGS}}

  mod-download:
    desc: Run 'go mod download'
    cmds:
      - go mod download
      - go -C clikit mod download
      - go mod download -modfile tools/go.mod

  dev-install:
    desc: Build from source and install to ~/.local/bin
    vars:
      DEST: '${HOME}/.local/bin'
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p "{{.DEST}}"
      - task: build
        vars:
          DEST: '{{.DEST}}/circleci'

    desc: Install known official extensions

      - go run ./cmd/circleci extension install testsuite
      - go run ./cmd/circleci extension install configoptimizer

  docs:reference:
    desc: Generate the reference page from the live command tree
    deps:
      - extensions:install
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p {{.SITE_DIR}}/content/reference {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/img
      # The landing page (/) is a hand-written template; the screenshot it shows
      # is the freeze-captured demo, copied into the site's static tree.
      - cp docs/demos/run-get.svg {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/img/run-get.svg
      # Generate the help-topic bodies once, then derive three artifacts:
      #
      #   static/llms.txt             — the short index llmstxt.org actually
      #                                 describes: getting started (install,
      #                                 authenticate, MCP), installing the
      #                                 agent skills, plus links out. This
      #                                 file used to be the full dump, which cost
      #                                 an agent ~50k tokens to answer "how do I
      #                                 install this?" — and then sent it to the
      #                                 README anyway. Keep it small.
      #   static/llms-full.txt        — every topic plus the whole command tree,
      #                                 for agents that need command detail.
      #   content/reference/_index.md — the same full body with Hugo front

        REST="$(mktemp)"
        {
          go run ./cmd/circleci help getting-started
          echo
          go run ./cmd/circleci help agents
        } > "$INTRO"
        {
          go run ./cmd/circleci help environment
          echo
          go run ./cmd/circleci help formatting
          echo
          go run ./cmd/circleci help reference
        } > "$REST"

        {
          echo '# CircleCI CLI'
          echo
          echo '> Command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or scripts. This is the short index: install, authenticate, install the agent skills, and links to the full reference.'

          cat "$INTRO"
          echo
          echo '## Reference'
          echo
          echo '- [Full command reference](https://cli.circleci.com/llms-full.txt): every command, flag and JSON field, generated from the live command tree. Large — fetch it when you need command detail.'

          echo '- [Environment variables](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#environment): authentication, colour, paging and telemetry. Also `circleci help environment`.'
          echo '- [Output formatting](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#formatting): `--json`, `--jq` and templates. Also `circleci help formatting`.'
          echo '- [Source, issue tracker and prebuilt binaries](https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli)'
        } > {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/llms.txt

        {
          echo '# CircleCI CLI'
          echo
          echo '> Command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or scripts. This is the full command reference, generated from the live command tree. The short index is at https://cli.circleci.com/llms.txt'
          echo
          cat "$INTRO"
          echo
          cat "$REST"
        } > {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/llms-full.txt

        {
          echo '---'
          echo 'title: CircleCI CLI Reference'
          echo '---'
          echo
          cat "$INTRO"
          echo
          cat "$REST"
        } > {{.SITE_DIR}}/content/reference/_index.md

        rm -f "$INTRO" "$REST"

  docs:clean:
    desc: Remove the built docs site
    cmds:
      - rm -rf {{.SITE_OUT}}

  docs:build:
    desc: Generate the reference and build the static site
    deps:
      - docs:clean
      - docs:reference
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod hugo --source {{.SITE_DIR}} --minify --gc'

  docs:server:
    desc: Serve the docs site locally with live reload
    deps:
      - docs:reference
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod hugo server --source {{.SITE_DIR}} {{.CLI_ARGS}}'

  docs:test:
    desc: Validate the built site's internal links with htmltest
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod htmltest -c {{.SITE_DIR}}/.htmltest.yml {{.CLI_ARGS}}'

  docs:hugo:
    desc: Run the pinned Hugo binary with arbitrary arguments
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod hugo --source {{.SITE_DIR}} {{.CLI_ARGS}}'

    desc: Publish the built site to the gh-pages branch (CI only)
    vars:
      BRANCH: gh-pages
      WORKTREE: .gh-pages
      MESSAGE: 'Deploy docs from {{env "CIRCLE_SHA1" | default "local"}}'
    cmds:
      - test -d {{.SITE_OUT}} || { echo "Run 'task docs:build' first."; exit 1; }
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      - rm -rf {{.WORKTREE}}
      - git worktree prune
      - |
        git fetch origin {{.BRANCH}} || true
        if git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/remotes/origin/{{.BRANCH}}; then
          git worktree add -B {{.BRANCH}} {{.WORKTREE}} origin/{{.BRANCH}}
        else
          git worktree add --orphan -b {{.BRANCH}} {{.WORKTREE}}
        fi
      # Replace the branch's contents wholesale so deletions propagate, then copy
      # in the freshly built site (the .git pointer file must survive).

      - cp -R {{.SITE_OUT}}/. {{.WORKTREE}}/

        git -C {{.WORKTREE}} add -A
        git -C {{.WORKTREE}} commit -m '{{.MESSAGE}}' || { echo "No changes to publish."; }
        git -C {{.WORKTREE}} push origin {{.BRANCH}}
      - git worktree remove --force {{.WORKTREE}}

  ci:lint:
    desc: Lint with JUnit output
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p "{{.RESULTS_DIR}}"
      - task: lint
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: |
            ./... \
            --output.junit-xml.path "{{.LINT_REPORT}}" --output.junit-xml.extended \
            --output.text.path=stdout --output.text.colors=true

  ci:test:
    desc: Run tests with JUnit output
    vars:
      NAME: '{{if not (eq OS "windows")}}ci tests{{else}}windows tests{{end}}'
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p {{.RESULTS_DIR}}
      - circleci testsuite run "{{.NAME}}"

    desc: Check no uncommitted diffs after generate/fmt/tidy
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: fmt:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: ci:lint
      - task: lint:clikit
      - task: license
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -check .
      - task: mod-tidy
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -diff
      - task: release-check
      - task: generate
      - git diff --exit-code

  ci:release-pr:
    desc: Open, update or close the release PR for what's merged since the last release (CI only)
    cmds:
      - go run ./cmd/ci/release pr

  ci:halt-unless-unreleased:
    desc: End the CI job, successfully, unless the release is untagged — its release PR was just merged (CI only)
    vars:
      VERSION: '{{.RELEASE_VERSION}}'
    cmds:
      # ls-remote exits 2 when the tag doesn't exist. Any other failure fails the job.
      - |
        if [ -z '{{.VERSION}}' ]; then
          echo 'CHANGELOG.md has no "## [x.y.z]" release section.' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        status=0
        git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin 'refs/tags/{{.VERSION}}' >/dev/null || status=$?
        case "$status" in
          0) echo '{{.VERSION}} is already released.'; circleci-agent step halt ;;
          2) echo 'Releasing {{.VERSION}}.' ;;
          *) exit "$status" ;;
        esac

  ci:release:
    desc: Tag, build, and publish the newest release in CHANGELOG.md
    vars:
      VERSION: '{{.RELEASE_VERSION}}'
    cmds:
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      - git tag -a '{{.VERSION}}' -m 'Release {{.VERSION}}'
      - git push origin '{{.VERSION}}'
      # The GitHub release's notes are the version's CHANGELOG.md section, which
      # its release PR added. Written outside dist/, which --clean empties.
      - |
        notes="$(mktemp)"
        go run ./cmd/ci/release notes > "$notes"
        go tool -modfile tools/go.mod goreleaser release --clean --release-notes "$notes"

      - task: ci:cloudsmith
      - task: ci:virustotal
      - task: ci:tag-clikit

  ci:tag-clikit:
    desc: Tag the clikit module so extension authors can 'go get' this release
    vars:
      TAG: 'clikit/{{.RELEASE_VERSION}}'
    cmds:
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      - git tag -a '{{.TAG}}' -m 'Release {{.TAG}}'
      - git push origin '{{.TAG}}'

    desc: Submit the release artifacts in dist/ to VirusTotal for scanning
    # VT_APIKEY must be set in the environment to actually upload; without it the
    # step logs a skip and exits 0. Submission is best-effort and never gates the
    # release — VirusTotal frequently false-flags Go binaries. Set DRY_RUN to list
    # the artifacts without contacting VirusTotal.
    vars:
      DRY_RUN: '{{default "" .DRY_RUN}}'
    cmds:
      # Submit what users actually download: the archives and the Linux packages.
      # VirusTotal unpacks archives and scans the contained binaries.
      - go run ./cmd/ci/virustotal submit {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}dist/*.tar.gz dist/*.zip dist/*.deb dist/*.rpm

  ci:packagecloud:
    desc: Publish the Linux nfpm packages (rpm + deb) from dist/ to packagecloud
    # PACKAGECLOUD_TOKEN must be set in the environment (not needed when DRY_RUN is
    # set). Override REPO to target a different packagecloud repository
    # (<user>/<repo>); set DRY_RUN to validate without uploading.
    vars:
      REPO: '{{default "circleci/circleci" .REPO}}'
      DRY_RUN: '{{default "" .DRY_RUN}}'
    cmds:
      # goreleaser only pushes to packagecloud under a Pro licence, so cmd/ci/packagecloud
      # uploads the nfpm output to the public REST API instead — no Ruby CLI needed.
      - go run ./cmd/ci/packagecloud pkg push {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}--repo '{{.REPO}}' dist/*.rpm dist/*.deb

  ci:cloudsmith:
    desc: Publish the Linux nfpm packages (deb + rpm) from dist/ to Cloudsmith
    # CLOUDSMITH_API_KEY must be set in the environment (not needed when DRY_RUN is
    # set). Override CLOUDSMITH_REPO to target a different Cloudsmith repository
    # (<owner>/<repo>); set DRY_RUN to validate without uploading.
    vars:
      CLOUDSMITH_REPO: '{{default "circleci-deps/public" .CLOUDSMITH_REPO}}'
      DRY_RUN: '{{default "" .DRY_RUN}}'
    cmds:
      # goreleaser can't push to Cloudsmith without a Pro licence, so cmd/ci/cloudsmith
      # uploads the nfpm output to the public REST API instead. Every package is
      # published to the generic "any-distro/any-version" distribution.
      - go run ./cmd/ci/cloudsmith push deb {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}--repo '{{.CLOUDSMITH_REPO}}' dist/*.deb
      - go run ./cmd/ci/cloudsmith push rpm {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}--repo '{{.CLOUDSMITH_REPO}}' dist/*.rpm

  ci:build:
    desc: Dry-run a release — build a snapshot (incl. nfpms) and dry-run the packagecloud publish
    vars:
      VERSION: '{{.RELEASE_VERSION}}'
    cmds:
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      # Forced: the version is usually released already, and its tag may have
      # been fetched. The tag is never pushed.
      - git tag -f -a '{{.VERSION}}' -m 'Release {{.VERSION}}'
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod goreleaser release --snapshot --skip=snapcraft --skip=chocolatey --clean
      - task: ci:packagecloud
        vars:
          DRY_RUN: "true"
      - task: ci:cloudsmith
        vars:
          DRY_RUN: "true"
      - task: ci:virustotal
        vars:
          DRY_RUN: "true"
